Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said at his Friday press conference that Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Reece James remain sidelined for Saturday's Premier League clash with Leeds at Stamford Bridge, while Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens are also unavailable. However, Emiliano Martínez is available after his head injury and Moises Caicedo's minutes were managed while on international duty with Ecuador so he should be fit to play.
Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs
Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.
Just ask right-back Ben White, who - with Riccardo Calafiori on the left - has been an important figure in Arsenal's superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: "Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you've got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10."
Between them, White and Calafiori have contributed to six goals for Arsenal already in the Premier League this season (White: three assists; Calafiori: one goal, two assists). No other defender has registered more than three goal involvements so far. The Arsenal duo are a great illustration of the impact full-backs can have. But, with the position more demanding than ever before, how does each Premier League team deploy theirs?
Enzo Maresca confirmed Matheus Nunes and Abdukodir Khusanov are both doubts for Manchester City's clash with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. The City coach cut a relaxed figure when asked about the three successive league defeats his team suffered before the international break, believing his team are progressing nicely.
He said: "I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we won games, and I'm also not thinking we're doing everything wrong when we're losing games.
"We've played 16 official games and we've won 12, so 70 per cent. If you tell me this is [will happen] in the next 16 games, I will sign! My view is probably different from everyone else's view. For me it's just the beginning of something long. I'm very happy in the way we're working while also being concerned about the things we need to do better.
"It's a matter of balance that we need to improve. We review things. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend."
Pochettino will have element of surprise an Anfield, says Iraola
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Mauricio Pochettino will have a tactical advantage over him on Sunday because the new Manchester United manager is coming in fresh.
Pochettino will be taking charge of United for the first time since leaving his role as USA national team coach to replace the sacked Michael Carrick.
With little to go on as to how Pochettino will setup his United side, Iraola is guessing.
"We've faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at, and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage," said Iraola. "We don't have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don't actually know.
"The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don't have the references that we have against other teams."
One advantage Iraola could have looked to exploit was the drone footage posted on YouTube of Pochettino's first training session at Carrington, but the Liverpool manager was quick to criticise the YouTube channel that posted the video.
"They were sending me the footage yesterday, but I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn't be legal. It happened to Manchester United but it could happen to me in a training session in the future," he said.
"It isn't about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect."
United not planning legal action against drone operator
Manchester United do not intend to take legal action against a drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, but warned that anyone responsible for further incidents would face significant legal and financial risk.
The operator, who identifies himself as Colin but has not disclosed his full name, apologised earlier today for what he called a "total error of judgement" and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.
A club source told Reuters there was no security breach at the Carrington site and that, while it was unclear whether the incident breached drone laws, United believed it had breached a number of other laws.
The club source said the operator had done the right thing by apologising and removing the content without being contacted by United. Reuters
Pochettino finishes on a question about whether or not the timing is right for him to manage United by saying: "A club like Manchester United, you cannot turn down."
Asked whether or not he missed the day-to-day club of club management, Pochettino replies: "Of course. We were missing [the pressure] a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we like to smell the grass and try to help the players improve everyday. It's true that it's a different job when you're in the national teams, but at the same time you learn a lot and we are much better coaches now."
Asked whether he thought was fit enough, Pochettino says: "When we arrive, I think we found a group of players that we propose to do the football that we feel. To be brave and be Manchester United. It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field."
He adds that data, such as the running stats referenced in the question, needs to be taken in context and while it can tell a story it is not the whole story.
Hinting at the question that plagued Ruben Amorim about whether he is coach or manager: "I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager. It does not change too much."
However, Pochettino also makes it clear he expects to be a part of the recruitment process: "I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad."
Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes will remain as captain: "Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.
"We spoke yesterday, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually yesterday. I think I missed some injured players but in the next few days we will talk with everyone.
"It was very nice contact. It is important to listen to the players and what they need to say about areas on and off the field."
"I don't think too much about the past," adds Pochettino. "It is about building our own way here. Of course, we feel the support from the club and we start to work.
"The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday. We have been speaking to the players and the most important thing is to think about the next action.
"We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority."
Pochettino says his target, after getting over the jet lag, is to get too know the people around the club and his players. He adds that his target is to "try and from the beginning have an impact. It is important to have a positive impact, that is our most important job."
Pochettino is happy to be here, which is a good start. Asked how you create a culture, he says: "The players need to buy into the idea that we need to improve, that is our job. The job is to find a way from Sunday to perform and to start to get the results that that [United] historically need because Manchester United need to be in a different place than they are now."
David Moyes has confirmed Jack Grealish is "fit and available" for Everton's trip to Brentford on Monday, having missed the past four games through a combination of illness and for disciplinary reasons. Arsenal's Lisa Baum: 'I believe in us. I think it's all about the small margins'
Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn't know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.
Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.
"It was unbelievable," says Baum, speaking in a small meeting room at Arsenal's London Colney training ground with a maturity that matches her play. "Everything just went so quick. I just shot, my brain was just switched off, it just came out."

Fabian Hürzeler: 'I've never had the feeling of leaving. I'm not done'
Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton coach, has given his press conference ahead of the game against Hull, and explained how, when and why he punishes players for not being sufficiently committed to their counter-pressing:
Counter-pressing is a law for us. Counter-pressing is not a decision you can do. It's something you can do when you have a good day, when you have a bad day, when you're in a bad mood, when you're ready for a game or training, you can do it every day. It's a non-negotiable for us. If you have the feeling the players are not on it then yeah, in some moments the players have to run. But we use it more in pre-season. As long as I'm happy with the counter-pressing we don't need it.
Hürzeler says he's not worried about drones taking footage of his training sessions. "No, because we have an airport next to us. So if they put a drone up I'm sure the drone won't exist long, because it can cause some bad consequences. We don't have this problem. We have other problems, with the aeroplanes, sometimes with the wind.
With the Brighton owner, Tony Bloom, having suggested this week that he could one day move to Bayern Munich, Hürzeler has committed his immediate future to the club, saying he "still has the feeling that I'm not done":
To me it's a privilege to work here. And of course in my time here there were a lot of rumours but I'm always fully committed to this club. I never had this feeling of leaving, because the club gives me a lot. I still go to bed and have the feeling that I'm not done. I still think there's potential to get out of this team, to get out of this club.
Arteta bans Arsenal employees from picking Arsenal players in FPL
As one of the most meticulous coaches in soccer, Mikel Arteta likes to have every base covered in his quest to win titles with Arsenal. Turns out his players giving away squad secrets through an online fantasy game is an area he hasn't been able to control, reports Associated Press.
In the latest example of a growing issue for Premier League managers, Arsenal winger Christos Tzolis unwittingly gave away a clue that he would be returning to action after a month-long injury absence by selecting himself in his own team in the Fantasy Premier League game played by more than 11 million people worldwide.
That information was picked up by some of the fantasy game's eagle-eyed content creators and, sure enough, Tzolis was named in Arsenal's team the very next day for the English champions' 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.
Guarding team selections is a big deal in soccer - hence limits to the presence of media at practice sessions and the furore that erupted when Southampton was found to have used an analyst to carry out the unauthorized filming of opponents in training last season. So Arteta has taken measures to combat the problem, with The Athletic reporting that he has banned Arsenal's players from including themselves or their teammates in their fantasy lineups.
On Friday, Arteta spoke about the issue, saying it has had an impact "with Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well."
"Constantly they are asking me about the lineups as well because they want to know," he said with a laugh, before adopting a more serious tone. "It is a topic, a thing that is happening in our society right now and it's something new - we've haven't [previously] dealt with it. We need to put new things in place."
Arteta insisted that "confidentiality is something critical" for teams wanting to be successful. "Because it's about trust, about what you are trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret," he said. "And we'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen again."
Earlier this month, the BBC reported that an email was sent by Chelsea to its staff, warning them about the possible consequences of making team selections in Fantasy Premier League using their inside information about injuries.
That came after Chelsea striker Joao Pedro was removed from the fantasy teams of teammate Morgan Rogers and other staff members before news of an injury to the Brazilian had been made public. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso later said he was "not into the fantasy team thing," so was unaware.
Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract at Southampton, extending his stay until 2029. Eckert, the architect of the so-called Spygate case, which saw Saints kicked out of last season's Championship play-offs and begin this season with a four-point deduction, said he is grateful for the continued support of owner Dragan Solak, group technical director Johannes Spors and chief executive Phil Parsons.
"There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come."
Southampton, who are seventh in the Championship, five points off the summit, host Derby this Saturday.
The 33-year-old's previous contract was due to expire at the end of the season. Despite the well-documented lows of last season, has picked up 96 points since initially taking charge on an interim basis 12 months ago, at least 12 more than any other club across the period.
Álvaro Arbeloa: Calvin Bassey 'one of the best in the world'
Fulham's Álvaro Arbeloa has given his Friday press conference ahead of his team's visit to Manchester City, against whom they have lost their last 20 games, and he has heaped praise on someone who is likely to be very busy: Calvin Bassey, who has been linked with a move to Manchester United.
I'm going to be really clear: he is very, very important. He's one of our captains, and from the first day that I arrived and I saw how good he is, I think he is one of the best centre-backs in the world. So it's normal that there are so many teams that want Calvin - that, for me, is normal.
I think Calvin is really happy here. He's so important for us, he's one of our leaders. I think he's performing really well. The way that we are playing, I think he can shine because he's a defender that can defend in a high line. He's very aggressive, he's very good with the ball. For me, he's brilliant as a player, so I am really happy with him, and I hope he will be with us for many years.
Fulham is not a jail - everyone that is here is because they want to be here, because they are happy, because they feel important, because they feel loved. And, for me, this is the most important thing.
MLS business, then, and Jeff Rueter has been musing about Columbus Crew ahead of their play-off fixture against Inter Miami tomorrow:
The Columbus Crew have a more holistic operation than most in MLS. The club as a whole still exists thanks to the dogged efforts of their fervent fanbase that helped block relocation. Their under-19s won the national cup in June, while the developmental Crew 2 made a fourth semi-final berth in five seasons in MLS Next Pro. The first team regularly punches above its weight in MLS, winning the third-most major titles (nine) among MLS originals.
And yet, this year tested the conventions set by team and league alike.
In January, chief soccer officer Issa Tall welcomed the club's eighth head coach, Henrik Rydström. Having only previously coached in his native Sweden, the 50-year-old used his introductory presser to laud the values of relationism, to praise his predecessor, and to plot a bold course for a new Crew. It was assumed he'd be around a while - the Crew have historically been patient with coaches, needing only seven bosses to navigate their first 30 seasons.
By mid-May, after just 16 games in charge, Rydström was on his way back to Sweden. His five wins were the lowest of the eight full-time Crew coaches. And yet, Saturday sees the Crew begin the MLS Cup Playoffs in a best-of-three matchup with Lionel Messi and Inter Miami.
Here's the Associated Press take on that Uefa draw:
Spain will face France in the Nations League quarter-finals in a rematch of their World Cup semi-final. England will play Norway in another World Cup rematch, but another matchup between Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé was the standout prospect from the Nations League draw made Friday.
Spain beat France 2-0 in July on its way to a World Cup title. England beat Norway 2-1 in the quarter-finals. The other quarterfinal pairings Friday were the Netherlands against title holder Portugal and Belgium against Germany.
The winners advance to the Final Four mini tournament from 9-13 June to be hosted by one of the teams. The host should be decided on 7 December at Uefa's executive committee meeting in Belfast, Northern Ireland.
These quarter-finals have been set a high bar by the previous edition in March 2025. Then, three of the four quarterfinals went to extra time in the second leg - two to penalty shootouts - and included 3-3 draws between Spain and the Netherlands and Germany against Italy, when the Italians trailed 3-0 at halftime. Portugal advanced to the Final Four by beating Denmark 5-2 after extra time in the second leg.
Belarus was drawn to play Israel in the promotion-relegation playoffs for a place in second tier League B. Neither team has played games on home soil for at least the last three years for security and political reasons. Current Uefa rules mean each must choose a neutral venue for their "home" leg, which opens the possibility of playing both games in the same stadium back-to-back.
Back to matters domestic, then, and Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann has spoken about the "insane" pressure heaped on coaches and players in the Scottish Premiership as he prepares to face Aberdeen in the wake of Stephen Robinson's dismissal, writes the Press Association.
Robinson arrived on the back of sustained success with Motherwell and St Mirren but barely got out of November in his first full season at Pittodrie. Killie sit bottom of the Premiership, two points behind the Dons, who travel to Rugby Park with former Vaduz and Luzern head coach Mario Frick at the helm.
"The pressures are insane at times," McCann said. "I just feel it was a tough situation for Stevie. He's a really good coach and I was really sad to see him lose his job. I suppose that's where we are in football. There seems to be a real appetite for applying pressure these days.
"You've got to be brave to be a professional athlete these days. There's a lot of scrutiny now. How people consume their media is very different to when I played. Everybody's got an opinion and it's quite vocal as well because it's accessible more than ever now, even to the players.
"I ask the players not to get involved in it but it's not like my time, there is an acceptance that there will be more to take in there. Maybe that's where the extra pressure's coming from. The external noise can't affect the game. If you let it affect you, then that's down to you."

Here's Ed Aarons with more on Arsenal's fitness issues:
Mikel Arteta has admitted Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury.
Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he is expected to be out for another four weeks.
When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. "I cannot be that specific," he said. "In four weeks' time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five."
Saliba back for Arsenal, Saka still four weeks from return
Mikel Arteta has given an update on the fitness of his players ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle, with the centre back William Saliba available after recovering from a back injury sustained during the World Cup but Martin Zubimendi out with a hamstring injury.
Saliba was forced off the field during France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain in July, and underwent a long rehabilitation programme. The 25-year-old appeared for Arsenal's Under-21 side earlier this month, and recently played a friendly against Watford behind closed doors.
"He's ready. He's in a good condition. He played two games, one behind closed doors and one more official and he did really well," Arteta told a press conference.
Arsenal have excelled in Saliba's absence, with close-season signing Ezri Konsa slotting in alongside Gabriel at the heart of the defence.
The Frenchman was a standout performer in their run to the Premier League title last season, but is not guaranteed to immediately reclaim his place in an Arsenal defence that has conceded only five goals in 10 league games this season.
Arsenal, however, will be without defensive midfielder Zubimendi for a few weeks after the Spain international suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's Nations League clash with England.
"He's out, he has a slight problem in his hamstring. But after the MRI scan there is an injury and he's going to be out for a few weeks," Arteta added.
Winger Bukayo Saka, who is out with a quadriceps injury, is still four weeks away from a possible return, the manager confirmed
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution, reports the Press Association.
Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo's former club Bournemouth at Anfield on August 15 last year.
But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: "Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case."
District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.
Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.
The court had heard Mr Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer. Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mr Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.
Mr Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in an interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to "hurry up". Mr Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

A drone operator who filmed Manchester United's training session this week has apologised for what he called a "total error of judgment" and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.
The footage, filmed at United's Carrington training ground during new manager Mauricio Pochettino's first training session on Thursday, was uploaded online under the username CC Overview. In a statement posted on his YouTube channel on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight was legal under drone regulations, filming the session had been "unethical".
"My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time," he said. "I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match."
The operator added that he had wrongly assumed only warm-up activities would be visible and that the training session would be open to various media outlets. He also said neither Liverpool nor any other football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington. "The video has been removed from my channel," he said.
Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott's return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys... here are your 10 things to look out for in the Premier League this weekend:
Fifa news ... Kozo Tashima said he hasn't talked yet with fellow Fifa presidential race challenfer Philippe Diallo, but he's willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino's bid for a controversial fourth term.
Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infantino in an election set for 18 March. So there's still plenty time to sway Fifa's 211 member federations.
"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," Tashima said in comments translated from Japanese. "I'm not looking at Diallo as opposition. I just want to change Fifa. Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management. I do trust him. At this point I'm not think about withdrawing."
Tashima, who repeated the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" when asked why he decided to stand, is going against the endorsement of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), which last month pledged support for Infantino - with Infantino on hand at the meeting in Tokyo.
"I just don't only want to be the Fifa president, my intention was to make Fifa better," Tashima added. "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organisation.
"I believe the worst outcome would be for him (Infantino) to remain in office without an election," he said. "I believe this is a test of whether Fifa truly has the capacity for self-reform. "He's done a lot of things to make us doubt his integrity," Tashima said, adding that income from the World Cup - or anywhere else - "is not an Infantino asset. It belongs to Fifa."
In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. For the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and a simple majority will win. In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need votes from 106 of the 211 member federations to win re-election.
Drone footage of Pochettino's first training session posted on YouTube
Footage from Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United manager has appeared online after being captured by a drone operator. A 12-minute video of the session was posted on to YouTube by an account called CC OVERVIEW after being captured at United's Carrington training ground. Pochettino and his United players can be seen in the video, with the squad having been divided into three groups.
On the post, the drone operator wrote: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
"The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
Manchester United have declined to comment.
Pochettino was taking his first training session after being appointed as United's new head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked with the club in the relegation zone during this international window. Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, having taken charge of the United States for the final time in their 2-0 win over Haiti, which finished in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. His first match in charge will be a visit to old rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. Press Association

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Mauricio Pochettino will have a tactical advantage over him on Sunday because the new Manchester United manager is coming in fresh.

With little to go on as to how Pochettino will setup his United side, Iraola is guessing.

"It isn't about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect."

A club source told Reuters there was no security breach at the Carrington site and that, while it was unclear whether the incident breached drone laws, United believed it had breached a number of other laws.
The club source said the operator had done the right thing by apologising and removing the content without being contacted by United. Reuters
Pochettino finishes on a question about whether or not the timing is right for him to manage United by saying: "A club like Manchester United, you cannot turn down."

It's true that it's a different job when you're in the national teams, but at the same time you learn a lot and we are much better coaches now."

He adds that data, such as the running stats referenced in the question, needs to be taken in context and while it can tell a story it is not the whole story.
Hinting at the question that plagued Ruben Amorim about whether he is coach or manager: "I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager. It does not change too much."

"We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority."

Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn't know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton coach, has given his press conference ahead of the game against Hull, and explained how, when and why he punishes players for not being sufficiently committed to their counter-pressing:
Counter-pressing is a law for us. Counter-pressing is not a decision you can do. It's something you can do when you have a good day, when you have a bad day, when you're in a bad mood, when you're ready for a game or training, you can do it every day. It's a non-negotiable for us. If you have the feeling the players are not on it then yeah, in some moments the players have to run. But we use it more in pre-season. As long as I'm happy with the counter-pressing we don't need it.
Hürzeler says he's not worried about drones taking footage of his training sessions. "No, because we have an airport next to us. So if they put a drone up I'm sure the drone won't exist long, because it can cause some bad consequences. We don't have this problem. We have other problems, with the aeroplanes, sometimes with the wind.
With the Brighton owner, Tony Bloom, having suggested this week that he could one day move to Bayern Munich, Hürzeler has committed his immediate future to the club, saying he "still has the feeling that I'm not done":
To me it's a privilege to work here. And of course in my time here there were a lot of rumours but I'm always fully committed to this club. I never had this feeling of leaving, because the club gives me a lot. I still go to bed and have the feeling that I'm not done. I still think there's potential to get out of this team, to get out of this club.

Arteta insisted that "confidentiality is something critical" for teams wanting to be successful.
